subject: Re: MAP - Data handling & compliance milestone (retention, logging, PHI/PII)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@medsyshealth.com>, security@medsyshealth.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: MAP Draft — Data handling & compliance milestone (post-call recap)

Hi Elaine / MedSys team,

Thanks again for the call today — great to understand your data classification and HIPAA adjacency. Attached is a first-pass MAP (MAP_draft_v1.xlsx) with the milestone we discussed around data handling and compliance. Below is the short recap and proposed milestone details so we have a single source of truth. Please confirm or flag edits.

MAP milestone — Data handling & compliance (proposed)
- Objective: Ensure Redwood deployment and controls meet MedSys requirements for PHI/PII handling, retention, logging, and auditability so legal/procurement can sign off.
- Target close date: 2026-04-15 (tentative — we know you have an internal review)
- Responsibilities:
  - MedSys: provide data classification guidance (PHI vs non-PHI), retention windows, required redaction rules, and security questionnaire (if any).
  - Redwood: provide SOC 2 attestation, data flow diagram, logging/audit schema, configuration options for retention / redaction, and BAA template for legal review.
- Dependencies: internal legal review at MedSys, procurement timeline, and access to a sample (sanitized) request/response log for integration testing.
- Success criteria: legal sign-off (BAA) and security sign-off (evidence of SOC 2 + logging/audit policy); staging PoC demonstrates redaction/retention settings working on a subset of traffic.

Next steps (action items)
1) MedSys: share security questionnaire / retention policy (ETA: one week)
2) Redwood (Vivek): share data flow diagram and SOC2 attestation + brief on redaction options (ETA: 3 business days)
3) Both: align on target close date and procurement milestones — I captured a proposed timeline in the attachment.

Attachments: MAP_draft_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestone table)

If that looks right, I'll get Vivek to share the technical docs and we can update the MAP.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@medsyshealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medsyshealth.com, procurement@medsyshealth.com
Date: 2026-03-19T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP Draft — Data handling & compliance milestone (post-call recap)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap and the MAP — looks good as a starting point. A few clarifying questions from our security and legal teams before we lock the milestone dates:

1) PHI handling: Will Redwood ever persist PHI on shared infrastructure? We need confirmation of deployment modes that would be used for PHI (hosted vs private).
2) BAA: Does Redwood sign a HIPAA BAA, and can you share a redlineable draft?
3) Retention controls: We need per-account retention TTLs (ability to set 30/90/365 day windows) and a way to purge data on-demand.
4) Logging / audit trail: We need field-level audit logs for all inference calls (timestamp, request id, model id, user/tenant id) retained for 1 year and exportable for audits.
5) Data residency: all PHI must remain in us-east-1 for our initial rollout.

I've attached our procurement timeline for reference. Can Vivek or someone on the eng/security side provide the SOC2 and a data flow diagram showing where data is stored/processed?

We may need to push the target close date by a week depending on legal's availability.

Best,
Elaine Morris
Director, Security & Compliance | MedSys Health
elaine.morris@medsyshealth.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@medsyshealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP Draft — Data handling & compliance milestone (technical follow-up)

Hi Elaine — thanks for the detail. Quick answers and what we can deliver this week: 

1) PHI persistence / deployment modes:
- Redwood Hosted (shared tenants): we recommend against storing PHI on shared-hosted for regulated workloads.
- Redwood Private (VPC / dedicated capacity or on-prem): supports PHI — data resides in customer-managed VPC or dedicated cluster in a single region. For MedSys we will plan a Private deployment in us-east-1.

2) BAA:
- Redwood does sign BAAs for enterprise customers for Private deployments. I'll flag legal to send a redlineable BAA template; ETA: 2 business days.

3) Retention controls / purge:
- Per-account retention TTLs are configurable at the project level (30 / 90 / 365 / custom). On-demand purge: we expose an API to delete persisted request logs and cached prefixes; deletion requests are propagated to storage within 24 hours and logged.

4) Logging / audit trail:
- We provide per-request audit metadata (timestamp, request_id, model_version, tenant_id, route) and can retain logs for configurable windows. Export: daily export to a customer S3 bucket or secure transfer via signed link. For audits we can provide hashed request identifiers plus metadata if you need additional de-identification.

5) Data residency:
- Private deployment in us-east-1 is supported. All storage, KV caches, and logs will be contained in that region for the MedSys deployment.

Deliverables we can attach this week:
- data_flow_diagram.png (shows flow for inference, KV-cache, logging sinks)
- SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf (Redwood SOC 2 Type II)
- short tech note on redaction approaches (pre-processing, tokenizer filters, and differential masking) — pasted below.

Proposed MAP milestone (technical breakdown)
- Milestone: Data handling & compliance sign-off
  - Redwood deliverables: SOC2 attestation, data flow diagram, BAA draft, retention/purge API docs, logging schema, PoC for redaction on sample dataset
  - MedSys deliverables: retention policy, sample sanitized logs for PoC, legal procurement sign-off
  - Target close date (proposed): 2026-04-15 (available to move to 2026-04-22 if you need additional review)
  - Dependencies: Legal review of BAA, procurement approval, access to sample dataset for PoC

Technical note (redaction options):
- Pre-processing redaction: customer-side redaction using regex/harmonization rules before sending requests to Redwood (best for highest control).
- On-ingest token filtering: Redwood can run configurable token filters to mask or drop high-risk fields at ingest (suitable for sensitive attributes).
- Application-level PII replacement: substitute tokens client-side and rehydrate on return if needed.

I'll upload the two attachments and the BAA template to the Drive link Marissa shared. Let me know if you want us to prepare a short PoC runbook.

Thanks,
Vivek
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
